The work was supported by the NASA Fundamental Aeronautics Programs and the Advanced Ceramic and Composites Program.
The objective was to develop advanced thermal barrier coating systems with superior erosion resistance and thermal performance.

The key requirements for the advanced low thermal conductivity coatings include retaining low thermal conductivity (1/2 of baseline) at 2400°F, improved sintering resistance and phase stability up to 3000°F, and excellent mechanical/durability properties.
The researchers used a nano-structured tetragonal phase approach, including the development of new six-component coating systems with distinctive ionic dopant cluster sizes.
Examples of the advanced coating compositions include Zr(Y,Gd,Yb)O2 and Zr(Yb,Nd,Y)O2.
The erosion resistance was evaluated using a newly developed high-velocity burner rig system that can achieve Mach 0.3-1.0 particle velocities and heat fluxes up to 315 W/cm2.
The optimized multi-component low thermal conductivity coatings demonstrated 50% less erosion than the baseline at 2150°F.

The advanced coatings retained about 1/2 the thermal conductivity of the baseline at 2400°F and showed improved cyclic life, with the Zr(Y,Gd,Yb)O2 cubic multilayer coating achieving over 1000 cycles at 2150°F.
Surface sintering and impact-induced densification zones were observed in the advanced coatings under high-heat flux conditions, leading to subsequent spallation and erosion damage.
The CO2 laser-based high-heat flux rig was used to achieve heat fluxes up to 315 W/cm2 and thermal gradients of 200-500°F/mil across 5-15 mil thick thermal barrier coatings.
The high-velocity burner rig system could achieve Mach 0.3-1.0 particle velocities, accommodating increased fuel and air flow to generate higher heat fluxes.
The heat flux in the high-velocity burner rig system was characterized using an embedded thermocouple sensor approach, achieving heat fluxes up to 50 W/cm2 at Mach 0.7-0.8 conditions.
The researchers completed initial simulated engine erosion testing and 600-hour cyclic durability tests at 2075°F for selected turbine airfoil coatings.
The study demonstrated the capabilities of the high-velocity burner rig and laser-based high-heat flux systems for validating the erosion performance of advanced thermal barrier coating systems.
The optimized coatings showed excellent thermal conductivity, erosion/impact resistance, and cyclic life, highlighting the benefits of the nano-structured tetragonal phase approach.
